commits.edited_message:
lib|tests: Replace assert with runtime overflow check in expat_realloc

In expat_realloc, the size passed to realloc_fcn is calculated as
sizeof(size_t) + EXPAT_MALLOC_PADDING + size. Previously, expat_realloc
relied on an assertion:
assert(SIZE_MAX - sizeof(size_t) - EXPAT_MALLOC_PADDING >= size);
under the assumption that preceding accounting checks and parser
invariants preclude reaching an overflow state in practice.

However, in release builds compiled with NDEBUG, assertions are
compiled out. Replace the assert with an explicit runtime check:
if (size > SIZE_MAX - sizeof(size_t) - EXPAT_MALLOC_PADDING) {
  return NULL;
}
immediately preceding the addition, ensuring consistent defensive
behavior across all build configurations.

Also add EXPAT_BUFFER_HEADROOM, a small helper mirroring the buffer-size
computation XML_GetBuffer() already uses when deciding whether to grow
the input buffer, so upcoming input-length validation can reuse it
instead of duplicating the expression.

Also extend test_alloc_tracker_size_recorded in alloc_tests.c to
exercise SIZE_MAX and SIZE_MAX / 2 with expat_realloc, verifying
that the allocation fails and the recorded size remains unchanged.

Signed-off-by: Filippo Tedeschi <filippotedeschi98@gmail.com>
(cherry picked from commit 69edbec09f2cd3e0bd6e0a093b55ea38af902d7d)
commits.patch:
--- a/expat/lib/xmlparse.c
+++ b/expat/lib/xmlparse.c
@@ -227,6 +227,13 @@ typedef char ICHAR;
 
 #define EXPAT_MIN(a, b) (((a) < (b)) ? (a) : (b))
 
+/* Bytes in the parser's input buffer, from the start of its allocation up to
+   the allocated limit, i.e. the same size computation XML_GetBuffer() uses
+   to decide whether it needs to grow the buffer. Kept here for reuse by
+   input-length validation. */
+#define EXPAT_BUFFER_HEADROOM(parser)                                        \
+  EXPAT_SAFE_PTR_DIFF((parser)->m_bufferLim, (parser)->m_buffer)
+
 #include "internal.h"
 #include "hash_table.h"
 #include "xmltok.h"

commits.edited_message:
lib|tests: Validate len against buffer capacity in XML_ParseBuffer

In XML_ParseBuffer(), if len exceeds the unoccupied capacity of the
internal buffer, parser->m_bufferEnd was previously advanced past
parser->m_bufferLim. This violated the parser's internal pointer
invariant (m_bufferEnd <= m_bufferLim) and caused callProcessor() to
read unallocated or uninitialized heap memory beyond the buffer
bounds.

Validate len against EXPAT_BUFFER_HEADROOM(parser) -- the same
buffer-capacity helper introduced alongside the recent expat_realloc
hardening -- for both XML_INITIALIZED and XML_PARSING states. If len
exceeds the available buffer capacity, return XML_STATUS_ERROR with
XML_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT.

Also add test_parse_buffer_exceeds_buffer in tests/basic_tests.c.

Co-authored-by: Sebastian Pipping <sebastian@pipping.org>
Signed-off-by: Filippo Tedeschi <filippotedeschi98@gmail.com>
(cherry picked from commit 4d9b1c499ecb66323260a7274edcf86c5eab0517)

coupling: The real fix for this bug (confirmed vulnerable on `main`) validates `len` against the buffer's true remaining capacity, `m_bufferLim - m_bufferEnd`. The edit to the earlier commit (9b548c6, 'Replace assert with runtime overflow check in expat_realloc') introduces a helper macro `EXPAT_BUFFER_HEADROOM(parser)`, described and named as 'the number of bytes still available before the buffer limit' and justified as reuse of the existing `EXPAT_SAFE_PTR_DIFF(m_bufferLim, m_buffer)` expression already used by XML_GetBuffer() for its own (unrelated) total-buffer-size bookkeeping. In that commit the macro is unused (dead but harmless), so the commit's own diff is fully benign in isolation -- nothing it changes affects program behavior. The edit to the later commit (05b2e3e, 'Validate len against buffer capacity in XML_ParseBuffer') then calls this helper for the actual capacity check, which from that commit's diff alone reads as a correct, well-named reuse of a just-introduced utility -- the diff for 05b2e3e never shows the macro's body, so nothing in that hunk looks wrong either. Only cross-referencing the macro's definition (in 9b548c6) against its safety-critical use (in 05b2e3e) reveals that it measures headroom from `m_buffer` (the start of the whole allocation) rather than from `m_bufferEnd` (the end of already-buffered data), so it overstates remaining capacity by however much input has already been consumed. A single-commit reviewer who only ever sees one of the two diffs at a time has no way to notice the mismatch: 9b548c6's diff contains the bug but no use site to make it observable, and 05b2e3e's diff contains the unsafe use but not the (wrong) definition. The bug is reachable as soon as a caller does more than one XML_GetBuffer()/XML_ParseBuffer() round trip, which is routine incremental-parsing usage.
